title: tiered-contact-attenuation-and-slo-threshold-sandbox
content:
Summary:

This is a sandbox-level writeup for a unified notification policy UX that combines: tiered contact lists (primary, escalation, fallback), per-channel attenuation (quiet windows, rate-limits, backoff), and SLO-derived threshold presets. The goal is to experiment with language and wireframe affordances that let engineers express 'when to wake someone' without having to reason about raw burn rates or arbitrary thresholds.

Why this exists (pain):
- Teams repeatedly over-alert because they set static thresholds without context of SLO burn or noise budgets.
- Current console exposes only per-signal numeric thresholds and channel toggles; users ask: how do I map this to "page someone" vs "log-only"?
- Multi-tenant defaults and per-route overrides are confusing; escalation configuration is fragmented across pages.

High-level goals:
- Make severity mapping from SLOs explicit: derive severity from ratio of error budget burn / time window.
- Provide preset personalities (conservative, balanced, optimistic) that translate to concrete thresholds and contact escalation steps.
- Allow per-channel attenuation layers (quiet hours, weekday-only, rate cap per 5m) and visualization of expected pages per day.
- Give a preview simulator to estimate noise under recent traffic.

Personas considered:
- Platform engineer (owns tenant defaults, wants safe presets)
- Product SRE (owns SLOs and wants tight burn-based paging)
- App engineer (wants simple toggles to avoid 2am pages)

Proposed UX pieces / screens (wireframe notes):
1) Notification Policy Canvas (top-level)
   - Left column: policy header with name, linked SLOs (badge list), active preset selector (dropdown: Conservative | Balanced | Experimental)
   - Middle column: Severity mapping editor (visual bar):
       * Horizontal slider for time window (1m, 5m, 1h)
       * For each severity (Info, Warning, Critical) a colored band indicating when it triggers relative to burn rate percentiles (e.g., Warning = >10% burn in 5m).
       * Inline tooltip: "Derived from SLO 'p99-latency' burn. Click to detach and set absolute threshold."
   - Right column: Contact tiers editor with drag-and-drop cards: Primary, Escalation 1, Escalation 2, External PagerDuty. Each card shows contact avatars, delivery channels, min-retry interval.

2) Channel Attenuation Modal (per-channel)
   - Controls: Quiet windows (repeating weekly schedule), Rate cap (pages/hour), Auto-snooze after N bursts, Holiday overrides (import calendar), Cost-aware toggle (if on, suppress verbose channels for low-severity alerts).
   - Live estimate line: "This will reduce pages by ~67% based on last 30 days" (uses simulator).

3) Policy Preview Simulator (bottom sheet)
   - Upload or pick a historical trace, pick time range, run simulation. Output: expected pages/day by channel and severity, top contributing routes. Button: "Export simulation -> CSV / create ticket".

4) Defaults & Tenant overlay
   - Toggle: "Enforce tenant defaults" vs "Allow route override". If enforced, per-route policy UI shows a small badge and a button to request exception.

Sample mapping rules (textual table):
- Example preset: Conservative
  - Info: no paging, log-only for burn <5% over 1h
  - Warning: page email+slack for burn 5-25% over 5m
  - Critical: page phone+pager duty for burn >25% over 1m

- Example preset: Experimental
  - Info: slack only for burn >2%
  - Warning: slack+email for burn >10%
  - Critical: escalate immediate to oncall for burn >20% but use exponential backoff for repeats

Notes on language: avoid alarming words in preset names. Prefer 'Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive' but test with customers since 'Aggressive' sounds negative. 'Balanced' might be default.

Backlog grooming (rough):
- UX-1 (JIRA-1227) Wireframe Notification Policy Canvas (2w) - owner Claire - must include simulator hook - priority P1
- UX-2 (JIRA-1299) Channel attenuation modal + calendar import (1w) - owner Mateo - depends on calendar API work in infra
- ENG-1 (JIRA-1338) Hook SLO burn calculator to policy service (3w) - owner Ravi - needs schema for burn windows
- ENG-2 (JIRA-1340) Simulation pipeline prototype (1w) - owner SRE - low-fi first pass using 7-day rolling window
- Research-1 (JIRA-1351) Customer interviews: reaction to preset names and defaults (2w) - owner product research

T-shirt sizing and acceptance criteria (draft):
- Wireframe canvas: M - acceptance: can create policy, assign SLO, change preset, simulate sample trace
- Channel attenuation: S - acceptance: set quiet-window and save; preview changes in simulator
- Simulator: L - acceptance: can run against 7-day trace, export CSV, and surface top 10 noisy routes

Edge cases / open questions:
- Multi-SLO policies: how to combine signals when one SLO is burning and another is healthy? Options: max(burn) vs weighted average. Need product rule decision.
- Per-tenant legal/regulatory constraints that forbid SMS/phone for certain accounts. How surface enforcement? Likely an enforcement toggle on tenant admin.
- Cost-aware suppression: experimental feature; must include explicit opt-in with ROI estimate.
- Backoff semantics: do we use fixed retry windows or exponential backoff? Prefer configurable but provide sane default (3m -> 15m -> 1h).

Interaction details (quick notes to engineers):
- Severity should be derived server-side from SLO burn calculator; UI only edits mapping from severity->contacts and attenuation rules.
- Policy object model suggestion (server): policy { name, slo_refs[], preset_id, mapping:[{severity, contact_tier, channel_rules}], attenuation_rules:[], tenant_enforcement:false }. (This is for discussion — not a final schema).

Designer notes / wireframe microcopy ideas:
- Policy header help: "Policies link SLOs to people: they define when to notify and who to notify."
- Preset tooltip: "Conservative: fewer pages, longer notification window. Balanced: default tradeoff. Experimental: quick paging for early detection (higher noise)."
- Simulator CTA: "Run on recent traffic to preview how many pages you would get before deploying."

Draft acceptance criteria for initial alpha release:
- Create / edit / delete policy with name and linked SLOs (UI)
- Attach preset and modify contact tiers (drag & drop contacts)
- Configure quiet windows per channel (weekly schedule)
- Run simulator on a 7-day sample and show pages by severity

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Claire: produce high-fidelity mockups for top-level canvas (due 2025-01-24)
- Ravi: prototype server endpoint for severity derivation and return sample burn numbers (due 2025-02-07)
- Mateo: audit existing channel delivery code to ensure we can set per-channel rate caps (due 2025-02-04)
- Ava: schedule customer interview slots and draft script (due 2025-01-17)

Quick sketch of user flow (notes):
1) Platform engineer creates tenant default policy with Conservative preset.
2) App team clones tenant policy to route-level, toggles "Allow route override" and loosens Critical->phone to email only.
3) On incident, severity is computed from SLO burn. Policy mapping determines channel set. Channel attenuation suppresses paging during quiet window; simulator shows expected pages if this policy were active.

Unresolved UX tradeoffs:
- Should we show raw burn numbers on the policy page? Some users want it for audit, others will be confused. Maybe an advanced toggle 'show raw SLO signals'.
- How to present per-contact escalation timing (e.g., after 5 minutes notify escalation). UI could allow relative timers per-card but keep defaults minimal.

Other miscellaneous notes and links:
- Example customer ask: "We want alerts only on weekdays between 9-6, except for Critical errors." Need policy expressiveness to say 'Critical bypass quiet windows'.
- Look at PagerDuty escalation model for inspiration but avoid cloning their complex UI.
- Slack thread: #product-alerting contains prior feedback (see linked artifacts).

Notes to self: keep language simple, prioritize visual mapping of burn->severity. Next draft should include 2 small mock screenshots and 1 simulation CSV sample.
